title: AI visibility audit for ecommerce catalogs: find weak SKUs and decide what to fix first
summary: How to audit a large catalog for AI search, find SKUs with missing or weak product data and decide which categories and products to fix first.
body_markdown:
AI shopping assistants and AI search features answer product questions using product data: your feeds, and your product pages with the structured data behind them. Products with missing or inconsistent data are less likely to be matched to a shopper's question.


In a large catalog, many products have gaps, and fixing all of them at once isn't realistic. An AI visibility audit shows which products have gaps and which of those are worth fixing first.


## What is a catalog AI visibility audit?


A catalog AI visibility audit checks every product against the data AI assistants use to find and recommend products. It scores each product's gaps and ranks which products to fix first.


It's different from a brand-level AI visibility audit, which tracks whether AI answers mention your brand for a set of questions. A brand-level audit shows whether you appear. A catalog audit shows which products are missing the data they need to appear, so you know what to fix.


## What product data do AI shopping assistants use?


The[product data AI shopping agents use](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/product-data-for-ai-shopping-agents) is mostly the same data that already powers search and shopping: your product feed, and your product pages with the structured data behind them.


For an audit, what matters is that each product is described completely, and the same way, in the feed and on the page.


## What makes a SKU weak for AI search?


For a consumer electronics retailer selling headphones, laptops, TVs and chargers, these are the signals to look for.


Signal Electronics example Why it matters


Missing required fields Headphones with no brand or GTIN in the feed The product may not be eligible to appear at all


Missing detail attributes Headphones with no battery life, noise cancellation or Bluetooth version listed They can't match a question like "noise-cancelling headphones with 30-hour battery"


Specs buried in marketing copy A laptop's RAM and weight mentioned only halfway through a paragraph Specs in a table or list are easier for AI to read than specs inside a story


No use cases or audience Headphones with no mention of commuting, the gym or calls AI can't match the product to questions about who or what it's for


Generic selling points "Premium sound" with no detail on what makes it better Gives AI no reason to recommend it over similar products


Inconsistent data A TV listed as 55 inches in the feed and 54.6 inches on the page, with a different model number in the markup AI may describe it wrongly or pass over it


Copy copied from the manufacturer The brand's description, word for word, as used by dozens of other stores Gives AI nothing to cite your page for over another


No visible reviews A laptop page with no rating or review count shown Reviews are part of how shoppers and AI judge a product


Out-of-date data A spec or model number in the feed that no longer matches the site AI answers can describe the product wrongly


Unanswered questions No information on whether a charger works with a specific phone Shoppers ask AI these questions directly


## How do you find weak SKUs across the whole catalog?


For larger catalogs especially, the audit needs to run on rules so it covers every product.


1. **Define the attributes each category needs.** Split them into required fields, the ones a product can't appear without, such as brand, title, image and GTIN, and detail attributes, such as battery life and noise cancellation for headphones or screen size and refresh rate for TVs.
2. **Compare every SKU against its category template.** Work out completeness per SKU and an average per category.
3. **Check the feed.** Look at feed titles first, then GTINs and images, since Google's shopping results and AI features draw on feed data.
4. **Check consistency.** Compare the feed, the product page, the structured data and the image for each SKU, and flag any that disagree.
5. **Flag thin and copied descriptions.** Mark descriptions that are very short, or[duplicate product descriptions](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/duplicate-product-descriptions-seo) that match the manufacturer's text word for word.
6. **Score each SKU.** Combine the checks into one score, with missing required fields weighted most heavily.


## Which products should you optimize first?


For each product, look at two things: how much it's worth to your business, and how big its data gap is. Products that are worth a lot and have big gaps come first. In very large catalogs, it can help to compare categories first, then rank products within the categories that matter most.


That gives you four groups:


Group Which products What to do


Fix first Important products with missing required fields or wrong data Fix them by hand or with review


Quick wins Important products that already get search impressions but are missing a few details Fill the missing attributes and improve the copy


Fix in bulk Many lower-selling products with the same gap, often from the same supplier Fix the cause once with a rule or a batch update


Check later Lower-selling products that are mostly complete Re-check them in the next audit


Bestsellers come first for missing required fields and wrong data, since an error on a top product costs the most. The long tail matters too, but long-tail products are usually cheaper to fix in batches than one at a time.


## Which data can you use to prioritize?


- **Revenue and margin** by SKU and category, from your own sales data.
- **Search Console.** Pages that already get impressions are the easiest to move. Google has also added[reports for its generative AI features](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/06/gen-ai-performance-reports) , which show impressions from AI Overviews and AI Mode by page.
- **Paid search data.** Conversions by product show where demand is proven.
- **Site search.** Queries that return no results or poor results point to missing attributes.


## What about pages beyond product pages?


AI answers draw on more than product pages. They also cite buying guides, comparison pages, size and fit pages and support content, depending on what shoppers need to know before they buy.


So for each priority category, check the supporting pages too. For electronics, that might be a TV size guide, a headphones comparison page or a compatibility FAQ for chargers. If those pages are missing or out of date, the product pages lose the context AI uses to recommend them.


## How do you fix weak SKUs at scale?


Fix the patterns before the products. If 3,000 headphones are missing battery life, the cause is usually one supplier feed or one mapping rule. Fixing that source fixes every SKU it feeds, and stops the gap from coming back with the next import.


Then fill the remaining gaps with[product data enrichment](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/features/ecommerce-product-data-enrichment) , reviewing values for the fix-first group and approving the bulk fixes in batches.


## How do you know if the audit worked?


Measure two things separately: whether AI shows your products, and whether AI sends you traffic. These don't always move together, since a page can help AI answer a question without getting the click.


- **Re-score the catalog.** Completeness and consistency scores for the priority categories should go up.
- **Check AI impressions and traffic.** Compare AI feature impressions in Search Console, and visits from AI assistants in your analytics, for the pages you fixed.
- **Watch feed health.** Disapproved or rejected items in Merchant Center and marketplace feeds should drop.

## FAQs


### How often should you run an AI visibility audit?


Run the checks on every new supplier file, so gaps are caught before products go live. Re-audit your priority categories at least quarterly, and after major changes such as a new channel or a taxonomy update.


### Does an AI visibility audit replace an SEO audit?


No. A catalog audit covers product data. Page speed and indexing still need a technical SEO check, and so does[LLM crawlability](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/llms-crawlability) , whether AI crawlers can reach your pages at all.
